name: The CLI subcommands 'system install' and 'system uninstall' are confusing people

current_round.prompt: The CLI subcommands 'system install' and 'system uninstall' are confusing people because they only manage systemctl (on Linux; I don't remember the one for macOS). The authority for updates is the 'system update' subcommand. Therefore, we need to rename install/uninstall to something that reflects what they actually do.

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

findings.description: The plan does not explicitly update operator-facing installation diagnostics in src/tools/host/installation/state.rs, which would continue directing users to the now-unparseable ./r system install command.
findings.recommendation: Include runtime diagnostics in the rename and test that recovery messages use system service-install instead of the retired spelling.

result.summary: Update runtime recovery guidance as part of the otherwise complete service-command rename.

checklist.description: Replace the public CLI actions with `service-install` and `service-uninstall`, update their help and dispatch identities, preserve their existing port-scoped systemd and launchd registration and removal behavior, and leave the ambiguous old spellings unparseable and unadvertised.

Update the checkout launcher to recognize and delegate `system service-install`, retain only the release-binary bootstrap required before first service registration, and keep Git and source update authority exclusively under `system update`.

Change the installed-executable recovery diagnostics in `src/tools/host/installation/state.rs` and any related operator-facing guidance to recommend `system service-install` so missing or invalid release-binary failures never direct users to the retired command.

Revise the affected process and CLI intent pages plus installation and update runbooks so they distinguish installing Refine, registering or removing its OS service, and updating Refine while preserving the established document format.

Migrate CLI parsing, command-catalog, launcher, runtime-diagnostic, and service integration expectations to the new spellings, including explicit coverage that recovery messages use `system service-install` and the retired `system install` and `system uninstall` surface is absent.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P3 now explicitly updates the installation-state recovery diagnostics to recommend `system service-install`, and P5 carries that operator-facing contract into the focused expectations while ensuring the retired spelling is not exposed.

result.summary: Rename the OS service registration commands to `system service-install` and `system service-uninstall` so their purpose is distinct from the launcher-owned `system update` path, and carry the new names through operator guidance, documentation, and compatibility contracts.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan does not require any governance violation.

checklist.evidence: Replaced the public `SystemAction` variants with `ServiceInstall` and `ServiceUninstall`, updated help text to describe port-scoped systemd/launchd registration and removal, retained the existing installation-service dispatch, and added parser plus catalog/help assertions proving the retired spellings are absent.

Updated `r` to recognize and delegate `system service-install`; added a missing-only production-binary bootstrap so first registration works while an existing binary is never implicitly rebuilt; retained the fixed Git/source update sequence solely under launcher-owned `system update`; launcher integration tests cover missing, unchanged, and source-changed cases.

Changed missing, non-file, and non-executable installed-binary recovery guidance in `src/tools/host/installation/state.rs` to recommend `./r system service-install --port <port>`; focused missing and invalid executable tests assert the new command and reject the retired spelling.

Updated the Process and CLI intent pages and the install and source-update runbooks to distinguish product file installation, production-binary publication, OS service registration/removal, and source updates while preserving the existing document structure.

Migrated CLI parsing/dispatch, command catalog/help, launcher, runtime diagnostics, production-binary integration, runbook validation, and real-systemd source-promotion fixtures. Explicit tests prove `service-install`/`service-uninstall` are advertised, recovery uses `service-install`, and `install`/`uninstall` no longer parse.

implementation.report: Renamed the public OS service commands to `system service-install` and `system service-uninstall`; preserved port-scoped systemd/launchd behavior; made the launcher bootstrap a missing release binary only for first service registration without rebuilding an existing binary or taking Git/source update authority from `system update`; updated installed-binary recovery diagnostics, intent pages, and install/update runbooks; and migrated parsing, catalog/help, launcher, diagnostic, runbook, and systemd integration expectations. Exact verification: focused CLI/catalog/diagnostic/runbook tests passed; `cargo test --test production_binary_install` passed 9/9; deterministic full library verification passed 1000 tests with 6 ignored; owned Rust formatting, launcher syntax, and diff whitespace checks passed. Parallel `cargo test --all-targets` exposed one unchanged concurrency-sensitive source-promotion test failure (`queued` observed before `running`) in both attempts after 999 passes and 6 ignores; that exact test passed in isolation and the complete library suite passed single-threaded. Repository-wide fmt and Clippy remain blocked only by pre-existing findings in untouched files, recorded in verification.
